hook.text: Nano products expose people at every stage — manufacturing, use, wear, and disposal each release particles differently.

buildup.text: Nano TiO₂ in paint weathers into dust — outdoor degradation releases particles that manufacturing contained safely.

discovery.text: Lifecycle assessment tracks nano exposure from cradle to grave — identifying the riskiest stage for each product.

twist.text: Recycling and incineration create new exposure pathways — nanomaterials may transform into different particles in fire.

climax.text: Circular economy design now includes nano end-of-life planning — ensuring safe disposal and recovery.

punchline.text: Safety is not just the product — it is every stage from factory to landfill.

quiz.question: Why is lifecycle assessment important for nano products?
options: Nanoparticles only pose risks during manufacturing
Exposure varies at each lifecycle stage, and degradation or disposal can create new risk pathways
Lifecycle assessment is required by international law for all products
